title: Direction & Distance
summary: Compass-walking puzzles: multi-leg journeys with left/right turns, questions on the shortest distance back, the direction faced, the endpoint's bearing from the start, and shadow-based facing. Everything reduces to two signed running totals plus one Pythagoras step, and most answers are 3-4-5 multiples. Shadow questions add one conversion line (morning shadow West, evening shadow East). A written trace of headings and components turns the whole topic into bookkeeping.

subtopics.title: Direction conventions and displacement
subtopics.concept:
Direction questions track a walker on an invisible grid. Fix the conventions first:

- **North is up, East is right**, South down, West left; North-East sits between North and East, and so on for the four diagonal directions.
- **Facing North:** left = West, right = East. **Facing South:** left = East, right = West. (A 'left turn' depends on where you face — this is the number-one trap.)
- 'Towards the sunrise' = **East**; 'towards the sunset' = **West**.
- The **shortest distance** from start is the straight line joining start to finish — never the sum of the legs walked.

Computationally: assign each leg a horizontal and vertical component (North: +y, South: −y, East: +x, West: −x), add them up, and apply Pythagoras:

$$\text{shortest distance} = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$$

Most CGL answers are Pythagorean triples — 3-4-5, 6-8-10, 5-12-13, 9-12-15 — so a clean square root usually means you are on track.

formulas.name: Shortest distance
formulas.note: x = net east-west movement, y = net north-south movement.

formulas.name: Turn directions
formulas.note: Left/right are relative to current facing; about-turn is 180°.

tricks.title: Two-axis bookkeeping
tricks.body: Keep two running totals: EAST-WEST and NORTH-SOUTH. East and West cancel each other; North and South cancel each other. The endpoint is (EW, NS) and distance is the square root of the sum of squares.

example.q:
**Q.** 8 km east, 6 km west, 3 km east — how far from start?

**Sol.** EW: +8 − 6 + 3 = +5; NS: 0. Distance = **5 km, East**. (17 km is the total walked, not the displacement.)
example.solution: Signed totals per axis; everything else is one square root.

tricks.title: Triple recognition
tricks.body: When the two net components come out as 3k and 4k (any order), the answer is 5k with no calculation: (6, 8) → 10, (9, 12) → 15, (12, 5) → 13.

example.q:
**Q.** 6 m east, then right and 8 m south. Distance from start?

**Sol.** (6, 8) = 2×(3, 4) → **10 m**.
example.solution: Scan for a multiple of 3-4-5 or 5-12-13 before touching a square root.

mistakes: Adding the legs (total path) instead of the straight-line displacement.
Turning left/right as if absolute (facing South, 'left' is East, not West).
Mixing the order of components — direction of the displacement needs its correct sign on each axis.

subtopics.title: Direction faced and net direction
subtopics.concept:
Two sub-formats:

1. **Which direction is X facing now?** — pure turn-tracking. A clock-wise turn of 90° maps N→E→S→W→N; anticlockwise runs N→W→S→E→N. An about-turn adds 180°. Turn, update the heading, repeat.
2. **In which direction is the endpoint from the start?** — finish the walk, note the final (x, y), and read the direction from signs: (+x, +y) = North-East, (−x, +y) = North-West, (+x, −y) = South-East, (−x, −y) = South-West; a zero component drops that word.

Both take seconds *if* you write the heading after every turn instead of trusting memory across three turns.

formulas.name: Clockwise cycle
formulas.note: Every right turn moves one step along this cycle.

formulas.name: Anticlockwise cycle
formulas.note: Every left turn moves one step along this cycle.

formulas.name: Sign reading
formulas.note: Signs of the net components give the quadrant.

tricks.title: Write the heading down each time
tricks.body: After every turn, overwrite a single letter (N/E/S/W). Three written letters beat one mental chain — and if a wrong option appears, each written heading is checkable.

example.q:
**Q.** Facing West, a man turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Final facing?

**Sol.** W --90° CW--> N --180° ACW--> **South**.

mistakes: Applying 'left = West' regardless of current facing.
Counting a 180° turn as two separate questions' worth of turns.
Reading the *final facing* when the question asks direction-from-start (or vice versa).

subtopics.title: Shadow questions
subtopics.concept:
The sun's position fixes the shadow:

- **Morning:** sun in the **East** → every shadow points **West**.
- **Evening:** sun in the **West** → every shadow points **East**.
- At local noon (in India) the shadow points roughly **North**.

The standard phrasings, decoded:

- 'Shadow falls **behind** him' → he faces **opposite** the shadow.
- 'Shadow falls **in front / towards him**' → he faces **along** the shadow.
- 'Shadow to his **left/right**' → he faces perpendicular, on the stated side.

Convert to a sentence about facing first, then run the walk. Do not skip the conversion — answering 'which way is the shadow' instead of 'which way is he facing' is the classic half-error.

tricks.title: One-line conversion
tricks.body: Rewrite the shadow sentence as a facing sentence before doing anything else: morning + behind = facing East; evening + in front = facing East; morning + shadow on the left = facing South (shadow West is on the left of a South-facing person).

example.q:
**Q.** One evening, Ramesh's shadow falls exactly in front of him. Which direction is he facing?

**Sol.** Evening shadow points East; shadow in front means he faces along it → **East**.
example.solution: Shadow sentence → facing sentence → answer. Three words per step.

mistakes: Using the evening shadow direction (East) in a morning question.
Answering the shadow's direction instead of the person's facing.
Forgetting shadow-left/right flips when the facing flips.

subtopics.title: Position of one point from another
subtopics.concept:
'C is 5 km East of A; A is 2 km North of B — in which direction is C from B?' Two anchored statements chain into one picture: place the *reference* person first (B), attach A relative to B, then C relative to A. The answer is read straight from the sketch.

Care points:

- **Direction reverses with reference**: 'C from B' (C relative to B) is the opposite corner of 'B from C'.
- Distances may be enough for a diagonal ('how far is C from B?' → Pythagoras on the two components).
- With three or more people, name the sketch's axes once (up = North) and place everyone before answering anything.

tricks.title: Place the final reference first
tricks.body: Start the sketch with the person the question asks FROM ('direction of C from B' → draw B at origin), then attach the chain. The answer is simply where C lands on the page.

example.q:
**Q.** A is 5 km North of B; C is 5 km East of A. Direction of C from B?

**Sol.** B at origin → A above it → C to A's right: C sits 5 East, 5 North of B → **North-East**.
example.solution: Anchor at the asked-from person; the chain then hangs downward.

mistakes: Drawing A first when B is the asked-from reference.
Reporting 'C from B' when the question asked 'B from C'.
Adding distances that need Pythagoras instead.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Shortest distance between start and finish
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A multi-leg walk; 'how far is he from the starting point?'
pyqPatterns.approach: Net components per axis, then Pythagoras; look for a 3-4-5 multiple.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Direction of the endpoint from start
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A walk with left/right turns; 'in which direction is he from the start?'
pyqPatterns.approach: Track (x, y) signs at the endpoint; quadrant names the direction.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Facing X, turns right, then about turn...' — which way now?
pyqPatterns.approach: Cycle N→E→S→W (right); write the heading after every turn.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Morning/evening shadow behind/in front/left — find the facing.
pyqPatterns.approach: Shadow points West in the morning, East in the evening; convert to a facing sentence.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'A is 5 km north of B; C is 3 km east of A — direction of C from B?'
pyqPatterns.approach: Sketch with the asked-from person at the origin; read off the quadrant.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Two people start together, walk different routes; find the gap.
pyqPatterns.approach: Compute both endpoints from the same origin, then the distance between them.

solvedExamples.q: **Ravi walks 3 km towards North, turns right and walks 4 km.** How far is he from the starting point?
solvedExamples.solution: North 3 km, then right (East) 4 km: components (4, 3). Shortest distance = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = **5 km**. (7 km is the distance walked — not asked.)
solvedExamples.shortcut: (3, 4) legs are the 3-4-5 triple — the answer is 5 without computing.
solvedExamples.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish

solvedExamples.q: **Maya walks 5 km South, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left and walks 5 km.** In which direction is she from the starting point?
solvedExamples.solution: South 5 → (0, −5). Facing South, left = East: +3 → (3, −5). Facing East, left = North: +5 → (3, 0). The y-components cancelled; she is **3 km East** of the start.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Opposite legs of equal length cancel — only the East 3 km survives.
solvedExamples.pattern: direction of the endpoint from start

solvedExamples.q: One morning, a man starts walking and his **shadow falls exactly behind him**. Which direction is he facing?
solvedExamples.solution: In the morning the sun is in the East, so every shadow points **West**. A shadow falling behind him means his back is to the West — he faces **East**.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Morning shadow = West; 'behind' ⇒ face opposite the shadow.

solvedExamples.q: **P is 4 km East of Q. R is 3 km South of P.** In which direction is **R from Q**?
solvedExamples.solution: Put Q at the origin: P is (+4, 0), R is (+4, −3). Both x and y components are non-zero, signs (+, −) → **South-East** (exactly 5 km away, by the triple).
solvedExamples.shortcut: Anchor at Q (the asked-from point); R lands in the (+, −) quadrant.

practice.q: **Asha walks 6 m towards East, turns right and walks 8 m.** How far is she from the starting point?
practice.solution: Components (6, 8) = 2 × (3, 4) → distance = 2 × 5 = **10 m**. (14 m is the path walked.)
practice.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish

practice.q: **Vikram walks 9 km towards South, then turns right and walks 12 km.** How far is he from the start?
practice.shortcut: 9-12 legs → 15 by the triple; no square root needed.
practice.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish

practice.q: **Neha walks 12 m North, turns right and walks 5 m, then turns right and walks 12 m.** How far is she from the starting point?
practice.solution: North 12 and South 12 cancel completely; only the East 5 m remains → **5 m**. (29 m is the total distance walked.)
practice.shortcut: Equal out-and-back legs on one axis vanish; only the crosswise leg survives.
practice.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish

practice.q: A man facing **West turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise**. Which direction is he facing now?
practice.solution: West --90° clockwise--> North --180°--> **South**. A 180° turn flips the heading whatever its sense.
practice.shortcut: Write the heading after each turn: W → N → S.

practice.q: **A is 5 km North of B. C is 5 km East of A.** In which direction is **C from B**?
practice.solution: B at origin → A at (0, 5) → C at (5, 5). Both components positive → **North-East** of B (7.07 km away, if asked).
practice.shortcut: Chain from B, the asked-from point: up 5, right 5 → NE.

practice.q: **Sameer walks 8 km East, then 6 km West, then 3 km East.** How far is he from the starting point?
practice.solution: Net East = 8 − 6 + 3 = 5 km; net North–South = 0 → **5 km East**. (17 km is the walking total.)
practice.shortcut: One signed column for East-West; opposite directions subtract.
practice.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish

practice.q: In the **evening**, Ramesh's shadow falls **exactly in front of him**. Which direction is he facing?
practice.solution: Evening sun is in the West, so shadows point **East**. A shadow in front means he faces along it → **East**.
practice.shortcut: Evening shadow = East; 'in front' ⇒ facing the shadow's direction.

practice.q: **Facing South, Sita walks 4 km, turns left and walks 4 km, then turns left again and walks 4 km.** In which direction is her endpoint from the start?
practice.solution: South 4 → (0, −4). Facing South, left = East → (4, −4). Facing East, left = North → (4, 0). Net: **4 km East**.
practice.shortcut: The two South-North legs cancel; the middle leg decides.
practice.pattern: direction of the endpoint from start

practice.q: Two friends start from the same point. **X walks 3 km North and then 4 km East. Y walks 4 km South and then 3 km West.** How far apart are they now?
practice.shortcut: Both walkers from the same origin; subtract components, then Pythagoras (√98 = 7√2).

practice.q: **Kiran starts facing East and walks 5 km, turns right and walks 3 km, turns right and walks 5 km, then turns right again and walks 2 km.** In which direction is she from the starting point?
practice.solution: East 5 → (5, 0); right → South 3 → (5, −3); right → West 5 → (0, −3); right → North 2 → (0, −1). The x-components cancel; 1 km of Southward drift remains → **South** of the start.
practice.shortcut: Cancel East-West first (5 and 5); the leftover South 1 km decides the direction.
practice.pattern: direction of the endpoint from start

practice.q: One morning, Amit walks **10 m towards the rising sun**, then turns left and walks 10 m. In which direction is he from his starting point?
practice.solution: Rising sun = East: he walks 10 m East, then turns left (facing East, left = North) 10 m. Endpoint (10, 10) → **North-East** of the start.
practice.shortcut: Sunrise = East; facing East, left is North — (+, +) endpoint means North-East.

practice.q: **Rani walks 7 km North, turns right and walks 7 km East, then turns right and walks 7 km South.** What is her position relative to the start?
practice.solution: North 7 and South 7 cancel; the East 7 km survives → she is **7 km East** of the start. (21 km is the distance walked.)
practice.shortcut: Out-and-back legs cancel; only the middle leg counts.
practice.pattern: direction of the endpoint from start

practice.q: **Imran walks 5 km North, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 9 km.** How far is he from the starting point?
practice.solution: North 5 → (0, 5); right = East 3 → (3, 5); right = South 9 → (3, −4). Distance = √(9 + 16) = **5 km**.
practice.shortcut: Components (3, 4) reappear after cancellation → the triple gives 5.
practice.pattern: shortest distance between start and finish

practice.q: **D is 6 km West of C. C is 4 km South of B.** In which direction is **B from D**?
practice.solution: Place D at the origin. 'D is 6 km West of C' puts C 6 km **East** of D. 'C is 4 km South of B' puts B 4 km **North** of C. So B sits at (+6, +4) from D → **North-East** of D.
practice.shortcut: Anchor at D (the asked-from point); C hangs East, B hangs North of C.

practice.q: A soldier marching towards **North** is ordered **'about turn'**, and then **'right turn'**. In which direction is he marching now?
practice.solution: About turn: North → South. Right turn from South: South → **West** (right-hand cycle N→E→S→W).
practice.shortcut: About turn = +180°; right turn = +90° on the N→E→S→W cycle.
